ORBITALCARE  Astronaut Health Monitoring System

ORBITALCARE is a web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support the observation of crew health during space missions. In space, astronauts experience challenging conditions such as microgravity, isolation and changes in their daily routines. These conditions can affect physical health, so regular monitoring and presentation of health information are important.

The project provides a dashboard where users can view astronaut health information and access monitoring and history pages. It is developed using Python and Flask for the application backend, with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Bootstrap-based web technologies for the interface. 

The prototype also includes a demonstration analysis feature that produces simulated AI/ML-style results to illustrate how unusual readings could be highlighted. This is a demonstration, not a trained machine-learning model or a validated medical diagnostic system. The monitoring values are simulated and should not be interpreted as real-time astronaut measurements.

A NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset from the Inspiration4 research study, containing comprehensive metabolic panel measurements, has been downloaded and included in the project files as a research resource. Its CSV processing is not yet connected to the web application, so the dashboard does not claim to analyse those NASA measurements.
details:
ORBITALCARE – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

ORBITALCARE is a web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support health observation during space missions. Astronauts experience challenging conditions such as microgravity, isolation and changes in their daily routines, which can affect their physical health. Our project aims to make health information easier to monitor, understand and review.

How does it work?

ORBITALCARE provides a user-friendly dashboard where users can select an astronaut and view health-related readings. It includes separate sections for health monitoring and health history. The system also contains a demonstration analysis feature that illustrates how unusual health readings could be identified and highlighted. Currently, the monitoring values and analysis results are simulated. A NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset containing Inspiration4 Comprehensive Metabolic Panel measurements has also been downloaded and included in the project files, but its processing is not yet connected to the application.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The system demonstrates how astronaut health information can be organised in one place. It aims to improve the presentation of health readings, make historical information easier to review and demonstrate how technology could help identify unusual patterns. In the future, it could support better health awareness and assist research into astronaut health during long-duration missions.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the project using Python as the main programming language and Flask for the backend. HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Bootstrap were used to create the user interface. SQLite is used for database-related functionality. We used a computer and a web browser for development and testing.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of ORBITALCARE is its space-themed interface, organised dashboard and combination of health monitoring, historical records and demonstration analysis in one platform. During development, we considered simplicity, readability, ease of navigation, data organisation and the challenges of monitoring astronaut health in space.

ORBITALCARE is an educational prototype, not a certified medical system or a replacement for professional medical decisions.
